# orchestra_monitor (Resource)

A rule for which failures to group into one incident, and how that incident alerts.

`match` picks the events the monitor claims, `group_by` decides what makes two of them the same incident, and `action` says what happens when one opens. Where two monitors claim the same event, the one Orchestra evaluates first wins — see `order`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Group every Snowflake and dbt failure on the warehouse pipelines into one
# incident per pipeline, and page on-call.
resource "orchestra_monitor" "warehouse_failures" {
  name        = "Warehouse failures"
  description = "Snowflake and dbt failures across the warehouse pipelines"

  match = {
    integrations = ["SNOWFLAKE", "DBT"]
  }

  # One incident per pipeline, rather than one per failing task.
  group_by = ["pipeline"]

  action = {
    severity = "HIGH"

    alerts = {
      destinations = [{
        integration = "SLACK"
        destination = "#data-oncall"
      }]
    }
  }
}

# A threshold monitor: a single blip is noise, five in half an hour is not.
resource "orchestra_monitor" "flaky_ingestion" {
  name = "Flaky ingestion"

  match = {
    integrations = ["FIVETRAN"]
  }

  group_by = ["connection"]

  trigger = {
    count  = 5
    within = "PT30M"
  }

  action = {
    severity = "MEDIUM"
    alerts = {
      also_send_to_pipeline_destinations = true
    }
  }
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `group_by` (List of String) What makes two claimed events the same incident — grouping by `pipeline` opens one incident per pipeline, by `monitor` one for the monitor as a whole. At least one.
- `match` (Attributes) Which events the monitor claims: AND across dimensions, OR within a list — `pipelines` plus `integrations` means events from those pipelines *and* those integrations.

At least one dimension is required. A monitor that named none would claim every event on the account. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--match))
- `name` (String) Monitor name, shown on the incidents it opens.

### Optional

- `action` (Attributes) What happens when an incident opens. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--action))
- `description` (String) What this monitor is for.
- `enabled` (Boolean) Whether the monitor claims events. A disabled monitor is skipped entirely.
- `trigger` (Attributes) Open an incident only after this many events in a window. Supplying `trigger` is what makes a monitor a threshold monitor; without it the first claimed event opens an incident. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--trigger))

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the monitor was created.
- `created_by` (String) User who created the monitor.
- `id` (String) The monitor ID.
- `order` (Number) Evaluation position within the workspace, assigned by Orchestra: where two monitors claim the same event, the lower `order` wins.

Ordering is a workspace-wide operation (`POST /monitors/reorder` renumbers every monitor at once), so it is not settable here. Set it in the Orchestra UI.
- `updated_at` (String) When the monitor was last updated.
- `updated_by` (String) User who last updated the monitor.

<a id="nestedatt--match"></a>
### Nested Schema for `match`

Optional:

- `assets` (List of String) Asset IDs to claim events from.
- `connections` (List of String) Connection IDs to claim events from.
- `integrations` (List of String) Integrations to claim events from.
- `labels` (Attributes Map) Label matches keyed by label name (max 32). Each entry is a JSON path into the event and the values that count as a match. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--match--labels))
- `pipelines` (List of String) Pipeline IDs to claim events from.

<a id="nestedatt--match--labels"></a>
### Nested Schema for `match.labels`

Required:

- `path` (String) JSON path into the event.
- `values` (List of String) Values that count as a match. At least one.



<a id="nestedatt--action"></a>
### Nested Schema for `action`

Optional:

- `alerts` (Attributes) Where to send the alert. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--action--alerts))
- `assignee` (String) User ID to assign the incident to.
- `mute` (Boolean) Open the incident without alerting.
- `severity` (String) Severity to open the incident at.

<a id="nestedatt--action--alerts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `action.alerts`

Optional:

- `also_send_to_pipeline_destinations` (Boolean) Also send to the destinations configured on the pipeline that produced the event.
- `destinations` (Attributes List) Destinations to alert. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--action--alerts--destinations))

<a id="nestedatt--action--alerts--destinations"></a>
### Nested Schema for `action.alerts.destinations`

Required:

- `integration` (String) Notification integration to send through.

Optional:

- `body` (String) Webhook request body, JSON-encoded. Only valid when `integration = "WEBHOOK"`. The API accepts an object or a string, so encode either — `jsonencode({...})` or `jsonencode("text")`.
- `connection_id` (String) Connection to authenticate the delivery with.
- `destination` (String) Where to deliver: an email address, Slack channel, or webhook URL, depending on `integration`.
- `priority` (Number) Datadog notification priority (1-5). Only valid when `integration = "DATADOG"`.




<a id="nestedatt--trigger"></a>
### Nested Schema for `trigger`

Required:

- `count` (Number) How many events before the incident opens. Must be more than 1.
- `within` (String) The window, as an ISO 8601 duration — `PT30M`, `PT2H`, `P1D`. Must be longer than zero.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Monitors are imported by ID.
terraform import orchestra_monitor.warehouse_failures 11111111-2222-3333-4444-555555555555
```
